datePolicy: Editorial estimates at seven-day intervals preserve ascending source ID order from 2025-01-05. They are not researched upload dates.

sources.thesis: Choose API documentation tooling by operational context: REST Docs links tested contracts to flexible documentation, while Swagger can bootstrap visibility in poorly documented legacy systems.
sources.reason: The body is a technical comparison of API documentation, controller testing, source-code intrusion, and an incremental legacy adoption strategy; video references only introduce the question.
risks: Automatic transcription may garble library names, and some claims depend on code or UI shown on screen. The preference is conditional rather than a universal tool verdict.

evidence.paraphrase: Swagger annotations and configuration enter the production source set, which the speaker considers an intrusive cost of producing richer documentation.
For an undocumented legacy system, the speaker recommends Swagger for existing APIs and REST Docs for new APIs, then improving the documentation incrementally.

sources.enTitle: Swagger vs REST Docs: Choose API Documentation by Context
sources.koTitle: 스웨거와 REST Docs, API 문서화 도구를 상황별로 고르는 법
sources.enDescription: Compare Swagger and REST Docs by test enforcement, code intrusion, customization, and a pragmatic migration path for legacy APIs.
sources.koDescription: 테스트 강제, 코드 침투성, 문서 확장성, 레거시 API의 점진적 전환 기준으로 두 도구를 비교합니다.

sources.thesis: Repeated Manager, Processor, and Handler classes are refactoring signals because vague names often hide unclear or excessive responsibilities.
sources.reason: The source analyzes naming, single responsibility, layer sizing, and a controlled incremental state in software design, with concrete guidance for reviewing a codebase.
risks: The examples are illustrative and based on an on-screen project. A vague class name is a diagnostic signal, not proof that every such class is defective.

evidence.paraphrase: A project containing many classes named Processor, Handler, or Manager is described as having a code smell and likely refactoring targets.
A generic class that accumulates CRUD, search, and other behavior violates a clear single responsibility; its vague name can intentionally expose that debt.

sources.enTitle: Why Manager and Processor Classes Are Refactoring Signals
sources.koTitle: Manager와 Processor 클래스가 리팩터링 대상이라는 신호
sources.enDescription: Use vague class names as code-smell signals, then narrow responsibilities and right-size layers without denying necessary transitional design.
sources.koDescription: 모호한 클래스 이름을 코드 스멜로 읽고, 과도한 책임과 레이어를 점진적으로 정리하는 기준을 설명합니다.

sources.thesis: Keep module-specific exceptions inside their owning module and translate them at chosen boundaries so implementation dependencies do not leak upward.
sources.reason: The body gives implementation-level guidance for exception ownership, module isolation, controller boundaries, validation, and scale-sensitive propagation rules.
risks: Names of code elements may be mistranscribed, and the example omits some on-screen context. Exception placement still depends on module structure, business semantics, and system size.

evidence.paraphrase: A module should remain independently movable, own the exceptions caused by its implementation, and expose a module-level exception instead of leaking a client library exception.
The consuming code should decide where an external module's exception stops, translate it behind a boundary, and preserve each module as an intact unit.

sources.enTitle: Translate Exceptions at Module Boundaries
sources.koTitle: 모듈 경계에서 예외를 변환하고 전파하는 법
sources.enDescription: Keep implementation exceptions inside their modules and define explicit translation boundaries that prevent dependencies from leaking upward.
sources.koDescription: 구현 예외를 소유 모듈 안에 가두고, 상위 계층으로 의존성이 새지 않도록 변환 경계를 설계합니다.

sources.thesis: Automate layer rules only when scale or review constraints justify it; small teams should preserve room to reason about and revise architecture together.
sources.reason: Its central purpose is architecture governance: weighing compile-time dependency enforcement against team discussion, developer judgment, growth, and project scale.
risks: The speaker had not used the named enforcement tools and was uncertain about their names. The argument is opinionated and should not be generalized to regulated or high-risk boundaries.

evidence.paraphrase: The speaker treats software as a team activity and worries that stronger automatic layer rules can replace architectural thought, preferring looser rules by default.

Mechanical enforcement becomes reasonable for repositories with many occasional contributors or too little review time, while layer and component choices should otherwise remain team discussion topics.

sources.enTitle: Architecture Rules Need Team Judgment Before Automation
sources.koTitle: 아키텍처 규칙 자동화보다 팀의 판단이 먼저다
sources.enDescription: Balance automated layer enforcement against review capacity, repository scale, developer growth, and a team's need to reason about architecture.
sources.koDescription: 레이어 규칙 자동화를 리뷰 여력, 저장소 규모, 개발자 성장, 팀의 아키텍처 토론과 함께 판단합니다.

sources.thesis: Delay ORM associations that do not reflect shared lifecycle and core responsibility, keeping important entities small while storing searchable supporting data separately.
sources.reason: The source is a detailed software and data-modeling discussion of JPA associations, entity responsibility, lifecycle, query needs, table separation, and incremental design.
risks: The review, image, and tag model is an improvised example without full product requirements. ASR obscures some JPA terminology and the advice is intentionally conditional.

evidence.paraphrase: A core Review entity need not know about tags or optional images; adding every association makes the central entity heavier, so relationships can be deferred.
Associations are useful when lifecycles truly match, but indiscriminate additions turn an entity into a god object that owns unrelated comments, types, tags, and images.

sources.enTitle: Keep Core Entities Light by Delaying ORM Associations
sources.koTitle: 핵심 엔티티를 가볍게 지키는 연관관계 설계
sources.enDescription: Decide ORM associations by lifecycle and responsibility, separating searchable supporting data so core entities stay focused and adaptable.
sources.koDescription: 생명주기와 책임으로 ORM 연관관계를 판단하고, 검색용 부가 데이터를 분리해 핵심 엔티티를 단순하게 유지합니다.

sources.thesis: Treat an order item as an immutable purchase snapshot separated from the current product, and prefer status transitions or archival safeguards over destructive deletion.
sources.reason: The body addresses domain boundaries, database relationships, historical integrity, refunds, soft deletion, rollback data, and operationally safe persistence design.
risks: The illegal-product scenario is hypothetical and omits legal retention requirements. Soft deletion is not universally correct, and ASR garbles foreign-key terminology.

evidence.paraphrase: An order item records the product at purchase time and belongs under the order boundary; deleting it because the current product changed destroys that conceptual snapshot.
Hard deletion loses history about the removed product and affected refunds, while a blocked or deleted status can preserve the information and support later analysis.

sources.enTitle: Protect Order Snapshots with Soft Delete and Boundaries
sources.koTitle: 주문 스냅샷을 지키는 소프트 삭제와 도메인 경계
sources.enDescription: Separate current products from immutable order snapshots, preserve refund history, and use status transitions or archives before destructive deletion.
sources.koDescription: 현재 상품과 주문 스냅샷의 경계를 나누고, 환불 이력을 보존하며 파괴적 삭제 전에 상태 전환과 보관을 검토합니다.

sources.thesis: A professional developer earns trust by completing company work within a minimum quality bar, then improving the result and preparing for the next level of growth.
sources.reason: Its central purpose is developer responsibility and growth: it distinguishes technical study and external recognition from finishing useful work for one's team and company.
risks: The rhetoric about work and external activity is deliberately sharp and reflects personal experience. It should not excuse poor quality, unhealthy workloads, or exploitative workplaces.

evidence.paraphrase: The speaker defines a good developer first as someone who does the company's work well, completes it, then refactors and evolves it while maintaining a minimum quality line.
Doing the current job well is only the base; a developer should keep preparing the next step, but professional work still takes priority over development as self-image.

sources.enTitle: Developer Growth Starts with Finishing the Work
sources.koTitle: 개발자 성장은 맡은 일을 끝내는 데서 시작한다
sources.enDescription: Build professional trust by completing valuable work within a quality baseline, then refactor, learn, and prepare deliberately for the next step.
sources.koDescription: 최소 품질선을 지키며 가치 있는 일을 완수하고, 이후 리팩터링과 학습으로 다음 성장을 준비하는 태도를 다룹니다.

sources.thesis: Separate domain learning from technology experiments: launch domain projects with familiar tools, and isolate unfamiliar infrastructure in minimal projects with focused performance tests.
sources.reason: The source provides a concrete developer learning method covering side projects, service launch, technology evaluation, performance testing, and avoiding compounded uncertainty.
risks: Tool names are sometimes unclear in the transcript, and the performance-test emphasis is personal advice rather than a complete validation plan. Costs and cloud guidance may vary.

evidence.paraphrase: For domain or product-idea learning, the speaker insists on familiar technology, fast launch, and performance testing to discover the system's practical limit.
Combining an unfamiliar domain with unfamiliar infrastructure often produces progress in neither, so technology experiments should use a minimal single-module project focused on that tool.

sources.enTitle: Separate Domain Learning from Technology Experiments
sources.koTitle: 도메인 학습과 기술 실험을 분리하는 두 가지 트랙
sources.enDescription: Use familiar tools to launch domain projects, and isolate unfamiliar infrastructure in minimal experiments with focused performance tests.
sources.koDescription: 도메인 프로젝트는 익숙한 기술로 출시하고, 낯선 인프라는 최소 프로젝트와 성능 테스트로 따로 검증합니다.

sources.thesis: For paginated like counts, begin with a bounded group-by query and presentation-layer composition before adding counters, Redis, or distributed synchronization costs.
sources.reason: The body is technical guidance on query modeling, table responsibility, concurrency, pagination, caching, consistency, and scale-driven performance evolution.
risks: The claim that a 20-item group-by will not be slow is illustrative, not benchmark evidence. Query shape, indexes, skew, database load, and consistency needs can change the result.

evidence.paraphrase: Instead of updating a like-count column on the review row, fetch counts with a grouped query for only the IDs in the current page and compose the response.
Redis may become useful at scale, but introducing it early adds distributed storage, refill, synchronization, and operational costs before a measured need exists.

sources.enTitle: Paginated Like Counts: Start with a Simple Query
sources.koTitle: 목록 좋아요 수는 단순한 조회부터 시작하라
sources.enDescription: Count likes for the current page with a bounded query before adding counter columns or Redis and their added management costs.
sources.koDescription: 현재 페이지의 좋아요만 제한적으로 조회하고, 카운터 컬럼이나 Redis는 규모가 커져 필요할 때 관리 비용과 함께 검토합니다.

sources.thesis: Discover domain boundaries by comparing when concepts are created, read, changed, and deleted, then adjust groupings to the product's actual requirements and coupling.
sources.reason: The source teaches domain modeling through lifecycle analysis, cohesion, coupling, boundaries, and examples involving products, orders, payments, shipping, cancellation, and settlement.
risks: The examples are exploratory and explicitly not definitive domain models. Requirements are incomplete, and several spoken terms or states may be mistranscribed.

evidence.paraphrase: The speaker proposes creation, reading, modification, and deletion as the basic dimensions for sensing whether concepts share a lifecycle.
Write out the concepts, draw boundaries, and group only close concepts; the resulting lifecycle model has no universal answer because requirements differ.

sources.enTitle: Find Domain Boundaries Through Concept Lifecycles
sources.koTitle: 개념의 생명주기로 도메인 경계를 찾는 법
sources.enDescription: Compare creation, reads, changes, and deletion to judge cohesion, coupling, and boundaries among products, orders, payments, shipping, and settlement.
sources.koDescription: 생성, 조회, 수정, 삭제 주기를 비교해 상품, 주문, 결제, 배송, 정산의 응집과 경계를 판단합니다.

sources.thesis: Good engineering solves the current problem efficiently with available resources, measures the result, and adds complexity only as scale and evidence demand it.
sources.reason: The body centers on engineering trade-offs, resource efficiency, overengineering, caching, infrastructure, performance measurement, and experience across different system scales.
risks: Traffic and company examples are rhetorical rather than measured case studies. Minimal resources should not be read as underprovisioning reliability, security, or recovery needs.

evidence.paraphrase: Engineering starts by extracting the most efficiency from the servers and database already available, measuring that baseline, and adding technology only when growth requires it.
A small problem that one table can solve should not receive Kafka-sized machinery; repeated practice solving small problems proportionally builds engineering judgment.

sources.enTitle: Solve Small Problems with Proportional Engineering
sources.koTitle: 작은 문제를 적은 자원으로 푸는 엔지니어링
sources.enDescription: Measure what existing systems can do, solve small problems proportionally, and add caches or distributed infrastructure only when evidence demands it.
sources.koDescription: 현재 시스템의 한계를 측정하고 작은 문제를 비례 있게 해결하며, 근거가 생길 때 캐시와 분산 인프라를 추가합니다.

sources.thesis: Modernize legacy systems through small verified deployments that deliver value, simplify rollback, and expose progress instead of accumulating a risky big-bang release.
sources.reason: The source is an operations and delivery analysis of legacy modernization, deployment slicing, verification, rollback, business risk, team stress, and incremental value.
risks: Schedule multipliers and line-count examples are illustrative, not measured estimates. Some migrations may still require coordinated cutovers, so iteration needs case-specific design.

evidence.paraphrase: The preferred approach repeatedly verifies and deploys each ready API or concept, limiting uncertainty to a small change instead of an entire year of work.
Verification, deployment slicing, and rollback must be designed from the start; validating a year of changes at once can stall or prevent the release entirely.

sources.enTitle: Modernize Legacy Systems with Small Deployments
sources.koTitle: 빅뱅 대신 작은 배포로 완성하는 레거시 개편
sources.enDescription: Reduce modernization risk with small verified deployments, practical rollback boundaries, visible progress, and value that survives a paused project.
sources.koDescription: 검증 가능한 작은 배포와 롤백 경계로 개편 위험을 낮추고, 프로젝트가 멈춰도 남는 가치와 진척을 만듭니다.

sources.thesis: Begin legacy improvement by proving and deleting dead code, using runtime data and consumer checks so the smaller system is safer to understand, operate, and change.
sources.reason: The body gives concrete legacy maintenance and operations guidance around dead-code identification, access logs, database evidence, API consumers, deletion risk, and incremental cleanup.
risks: The named dead-code tool is unclear in the transcript and only partially observed runtime classes. Logs can miss rare or seasonal use, so tool output alone cannot prove safe deletion.

evidence.paraphrase: Adding code is easy but deleting it safely is hard; before remodularizing a long-lived unknown system, the speaker first removes code shown to be unused.
For APIs, inspect access logs over the longest relevant period and confirm actual use in consuming repositories or with owning teams before deleting the call chain.

sources.enTitle: Legacy Cleanup Starts with Safe Dead-Code Removal
sources.koTitle: 레거시 개선은 죽은 코드를 안전하게 지우는 데서 시작한다
sources.enDescription: Shrink legacy systems safely by combining runtime evidence, database checks, API consumer verification, and incremental dead-code deletion.
sources.koDescription: 런타임 증거, 데이터 확인, API 소비자 검증을 결합해 죽은 코드를 점진적으로 삭제하고 레거시를 줄입니다.

sources.thesis: Developers applying as entry-level candidates with prior work should prepare to explain what they did, the problems they faced, how they approached them, the solutions they tried, and the actions they took.
sources.reason: The source is explicitly developer career and hiring guidance focused on resumes, interviews, problem-solving depth, work attitude, transfer motivation, and evidence of action.
risks: This reflects one interviewer's preferences, not a universal hiring rubric. Market comments are time-sensitive, and the advice should not reward inflated ownership or invented scale tests.

evidence.paraphrase: Prior work changes the interview focus from general knowledge to what problem the candidate faced, how deeply they considered it, and how they worked through an imperfect solution.
Candidates should prepare follow-up reasoning about constraints and alternatives; independent experiments help only when they produced a concrete action and learning, not a hollow claim.

sources.enTitle: How Experienced Entry-Level Developers Can Stand Out
sources.koTitle: 경력 있는 신입 개발자는 업무 경험으로 차별화하라
sources.enDescription: Prepare prior work for interviews by explaining what you did, the problem you faced, how you approached it, the solution you tried, and the action you took.
sources.koDescription: 이전에 한 일과 문제, 접근 방식, 시도한 해법과 실제 행동을 면접에서 구체적으로 설명하는 법을 다룹니다.

sources.thesis: Replace universal dynamic query methods with purpose-specific operations, then migrate callers in small deployments that narrow side effects before deeper cleanup.
sources.reason: The source provides implementation and refactoring guidance on god methods, dynamic query conditions, naming, parameters, side effects, call-site migration, and incremental delivery.
risks: The sample code is deliberately reconstructed rather than the real proprietary code. Copying before splitting can duplicate defects, so characterization tests and call-site verification may be needed.

evidence.paraphrase: A single dynamic query used by many callers hides each call's purpose and makes changing one condition expose every other path to unpredictable side effects.
The remedy is to split the method by purpose, move callers gradually, remove irrelevant parameters, and first isolate the portion whose impact can be understood.

sources.enTitle: Split God Query Methods by Purpose
sources.koTitle: 모든 조회를 삼키는 만능 메서드를 목적별로 쪼개라
sources.enDescription: Replace universal dynamic queries with purpose-specific methods, migrate callers incrementally, and shrink the side-effect surface before deeper refactoring.
sources.koDescription: 만능 동적 조회를 목적별 메서드로 나누고 호출부를 점진적으로 옮겨, 리팩터링의 사이드 이펙트를 줄입니다.

sources.thesis: Reserve a disjoint identifier range for the new database during migration so rollback data can return without primary-key collisions and operations remain easy to distinguish.
sources.reason: The body is a focused database migration and operations technique covering sequences, dual-running systems, rollback, reverse migration, consistency, logs, and cross-system identifiers.
risks: Numeric ranges and the three-hour rollback scenario are illustrative. The source explains separation qualitatively and does not provide a formula for choosing the size of the gap.

evidence.paraphrase: Starting the new database at the legacy database's current sequence makes rollback collisions likely, so the proposed safeguard is to advance the new identifier range substantially.
With separated ranges, new rows can be copied back into the still-running legacy database without overlapping IDs even when both sides continued receiving data.

sources.enTitle: Use ID Range Gaps for Safer Database Rollbacks
sources.koTitle: 아이디 범위를 띄워 DB 마이그레이션 롤백을 안전하게 만들기
sources.enDescription: Separate legacy and new identifier ranges to prevent rollback collisions, simplify reverse migration, and make operational traffic easier to trace.
sources.koDescription: 레거시와 신규 아이디 범위를 분리해 롤백 충돌을 막고, 역마이그레이션과 운영 트래픽 추적을 단순하게 만듭니다.

sources.thesis: Keep engagement aggregates outside the core table, refresh them at the consistency level users need, and evolve from queries to async events or search infrastructure only with scale.
sources.reason: The source is an extensive technical treatment of aggregation tables, pagination, contention, eventual consistency, asynchronous updates, batch refresh, events, search separation, and scale.
risks: All traffic volumes and freshness intervals are illustrative. Eventual consistency is acceptable only if product semantics allow it, and the search-system discussion is high-level rather than an implementation recipe.

evidence.paraphrase: At larger data volumes, store like counts and other ranking signals in a separate metadata table rather than contaminating the product or review lifecycle with aggregate columns.
Updating an aggregate row in the primary transaction creates contention that can block the core like action, so asynchronous events and periodic reconciliation can isolate the secondary concern.

sources.enTitle: Separate Core Data from Like-Count Aggregates
sources.koTitle: 좋아요 정렬을 위한 핵심 데이터와 집계 데이터 분리
sources.enDescription: Design scalable like-based ranking with separate aggregates, explicit freshness goals, async updates, reconciliation, and search boundaries that follow real demand.
sources.koDescription: 집계 분리, 명시적인 최신성 기준, 비동기 갱신, 정합성 보정, 검색 경계로 좋아요 기반 정렬을 확장합니다.

sources.thesis: Seniority is demonstrated by leaving maintainable code, tests, guidance, and room for successors rather than by tenure or personal coding stamina.
sources.reason: The body centers on developer responsibility, team sustainability, testing, mentorship, and the legacy a senior leaves to later maintainers.
risks: The argument is delivered through an anonymized second-hand workplace account that cannot be independently checked.
The speaker's anger and categorical career advice should be softened and contextualized for publication.

evidence.paraphrase: The speaker says a senior will eventually leave, so juniors inherit the legacy created by that person's style, including oversized untested classes.
A senior's basic role is to help the team continue after departure by balancing successors' freedom with practical guidance and ongoing adjustment.

sources.enTitle: What Senior Engineers Owe the Developers Who Come Next
sources.koTitle: 시니어 개발자가 다음 개발자에게 남겨야 할 유산
sources.enDescription: Seniority is more than tenure: learn how maintainable code, tests, guidance, and team continuity define responsible senior engineering.
sources.koDescription: 연차가 아니라 유지보수 가능한 코드, 테스트, 가이드와 팀의 지속가능성으로 시니어의 책임을 살펴봅니다.

sources.thesis: The speaker introduces a newly built anonymous career community, outlines its features and deployment shape, and repeatedly invites viewers to join and use it.
sources.reason: Although the body includes useful architecture and privacy details, its central purpose is to launch, demonstrate, and recruit users for the speaker's own service.
risks: Claims of complete anonymity are not supported by an independent security or privacy review.
Several framework and architecture terms are uncertain in the automatic transcript.
Publication as technical guidance would require separating the implementation lessons from the service invitation.

evidence.paraphrase: The opening explicitly announces a new project, names the service, and introduces anonymous profile evaluation and community features.
The closing asks interested viewers to visit, sign up, post questions, and use the service while promising future examples from it.

sources.enTitle: Inside an Anonymous Developer Community Service Architecture
sources.koTitle: 익명 개발자 커뮤니티 서비스의 구조와 설계
sources.enDescription: A service introduction covering anonymous signup, profile evaluation, private backend access, separate frontend, API, batch, and database components.
sources.koDescription: 익명 가입, 프로필 평가, 비공개 백엔드와 프론트엔드·API·배치 분리 구조를 소개합니다.

sources.thesis: Guest-facing masking and author markers should be generated at the presentation boundary so UI policy does not contaminate reusable business concepts.
sources.reason: The complete body is an implementation and layering discussion grounded in two concrete backend response-shaping examples.
risks: The transcript describes on-screen code that is not preserved in the text.
The recommended layer boundary is explicitly conditional and should not be generalized to rules that are genuinely business policy.

evidence.paraphrase: The speaker keeps business logic pure and places guest masking in the presentation layer because it exists to satisfy a UI disclosure requirement.
An is-author response flag is treated as removable UI specification rather than an intrinsic comment field, preserving the inner model from presentation changes.

sources.enTitle: Keep Guest Data Masking in the Presentation Layer
sources.koTitle: 로그인 전 데이터 마스킹을 프레젠테이션 계층에 두는 법
sources.enDescription: Learn why guest masking and author flags belong at the presentation boundary, keeping domain logic clean while preventing raw data exposure.
sources.koDescription: 게스트 마스킹과 작성자 표시를 프레젠테이션 경계에 격리해 도메인 로직과 원문 데이터를 보호하는 방법을 설명합니다.

sources.thesis: An anonymous service can reduce account-to-profile correlation by separating identifier spaces, discarding temporary mapping data, and retaining only what duplicate prevention requires.
sources.reason: The source is centrally about data modeling and privacy-oriented implementation tradeoffs for a real service.
risks: The phrase complete anonymity overstates what the described design alone can prove.
The design has not been independently threat-modeled, legally reviewed, or audited for infrastructure-level identifiers and access logs.
The speaker acknowledges unresolved timestamp and recoverability tradeoffs.

evidence.paraphrase: User-side identifiers are strings rather than matching profile sequences, and no profile-to-user mapping is stored; login secrets are isolated separately.
A temporary key supports initial profile import and duplicate prevention, then the mapping data is discarded instead of retained in the database.

sources.enTitle: Reduce Account-to-Profile Linkability in Anonymous Services
sources.koTitle: 계정과 프로필 연결 가능성을 낮추는 익명 설계
sources.enDescription: Explore identifier separation, disposable mapping keys, minimal retention, and the recovery tradeoffs behind a privacy-oriented account model.
sources.koDescription: 식별자 분리, 휘발성 매핑 키, 최소 보관과 계정 복구 제약을 통해 익명 계정 모델의 트레이드오프를 살펴봅니다.

sources.thesis: A company supplies work and experience, but developers grow only by deliberately converting experience from work, study, projects, and communities into their own judgment.
sources.reason: The body is a developer career and learning argument about personal agency, workplace choice, and reflective practice rather than promotion or general autobiography.
risks: The opening uses intentionally provocative and dismissive language that could obscure the later nuance.
The claim that employers owe no growth opportunity is normative and should be presented as the speaker's position, not universal employment guidance.

evidence.paraphrase: Work, books, courses, projects, and communities provide experience points, but growth occurs only when a person combines and internalizes them.
The conclusion makes the individual responsible for growth while allowing workplace choice to consider whether useful experience will be available.

sources.enTitle: Your Company Provides Experience, Not Developer Growth
sources.koTitle: 회사가 아닌 개발자가 자신의 성장을 책임지는 법
sources.enDescription: Developer growth comes from turning work, books, projects, and communities into personal judgment—not waiting for an employer to do it.
sources.koDescription: 회사, 책, 프로젝트와 커뮤니티의 경험을 자기 판단으로 바꾸며 개발자 성장을 스스로 책임지는 관점을 다룹니다.

sources.thesis: Agile values do not excuse refusing documentation; teams should document when continuity, organizational needs, regulation, or security make it necessary.
sources.reason: The central purpose is developer collaboration and sustainable engineering practice, using the Agile Manifesto to reject false either-or reasoning.
risks: The delivery repeatedly insults hypothetical colleagues and requires substantial tone editing.
The transcript paraphrases the Agile Manifesto rather than providing a stable primary-source citation.
The source argues for context-dependent documentation but does not define a concrete minimum document set.

evidence.paraphrase: The source stresses that Agile values working software more, not exclusively, and rejects using that preference to abandon all documentation and comments.
Documentation is required when the team needs it, when company assets must persist, and when regulated or security-sensitive work requires evidence.

sources.enTitle: Agile Does Not Mean No Documentation
sources.koTitle: 애자일은 문서화를 하지 말라는 뜻이 아니다
sources.enDescription: Agile values working software without banning documentation. Write what teams, continuity, security, and regulated operations genuinely require.
sources.koDescription: 애자일을 문서화 거부의 핑계로 삼지 않고 팀의 연속성, 보안, 규제와 운영에 필요한 문서를 판단하는 기준을 다룹니다.

sources.thesis: AI-assisted coding can accelerate access and learning, but developers still need technical fundamentals, problem definition, quality criteria, and judgment to select and verify generated work.
sources.reason: The source focuses on responsible developer practice and learning with AI rather than promoting a tool or course.
risks: Predictions about AI replacing developers and future work are speculative and time-sensitive.
Tool names and the claimed origin date of the vibe-coding term may be mistranscribed or require current primary-source verification.
The movie analogy is incidental and should not carry the technical argument.

evidence.paraphrase: Choosing among AI proposals requires reading code, judging fit to the current situation, and retaining development knowledge and problem-definition ability.
The main risk is surrendering thought and quality standards; continued study turns AI from a dependency into a learning and collaboration tool.

sources.enTitle: Vibe Coding Still Requires Engineering Judgment
sources.koTitle: 바이브 코딩 시대에도 개발자 판단력이 필요한 이유
sources.enDescription: Use AI coding tools without surrendering problem definition, code review, quality standards, or the technical knowledge needed to verify results.
sources.koDescription: AI 코딩을 활용하면서도 문제 정의, 코드 검토, 품질 기준과 결과를 검증할 기술 지식을 지키는 방법을 다룹니다.

sources.thesis: Refactor opaque legacy code by first capturing its proven external behavior with broad characterization tests, then narrowing tests and shipping small reversible changes.
sources.reason: The entire source presents a concrete testing, refactoring, rollback, and incremental-delivery strategy for functioning legacy systems.
risks: The example is primarily API and local Spring-context oriented and is not claimed to fit every legacy system.
Production request and response logs may contain sensitive data and must not be copied into tests without sanitization.
Characterization tests cover observed cases, not every hidden behavior.

evidence.paraphrase: For tangled code, the first move is a large outer net: dense E2E or API tests that capture the currently working behavior before internal analysis.
Observed request-response cases become a safety net for refactoring, followed by partial traffic, rollback on failure, and gradually broader coverage.

sources.enTitle: Refactor Spaghetti Code with Characterization Tests
sources.koTitle: 동작하는 스파게티 코드를 특성 테스트로 리팩터링하기
sources.enDescription: Capture legacy behavior with broad API tests, refactor behind the safety net, and deploy small reversible changes while coverage grows.
sources.koDescription: 넓은 API 특성 테스트로 레거시 동작을 고정하고 안전망 안에서 리팩터링한 뒤 작은 가역적 변경으로 배포하는 전략을 설명합니다.

sources.thesis: Separate external data retrieval from internal transformation and persistence so processing bugs can be retried without repeating expensive or rate-limited API calls.
sources.reason: The source is an operations-grounded batch design case covering failure recovery, traffic constraints, staging data, retries, and job orchestration.
risks: The case is recalled from memory, and the speaker flags uncertainty about some implementation details.
The example's product counts and schedule gaps are illustrative rather than measured recommendations.
Staging raw third-party data introduces retention, storage, schema-versioning, and privacy concerns not fully explored.

evidence.paraphrase: The solution splits receipt from processing: store the external representation first, then load and transform it into the internal database shape in a second batch.
Once external calls are isolated, transformation bugs and mapping changes can be fixed by rerunning only the second batch without hitting the provider again.

sources.enTitle: Split Batch Ingestion from Processing to Reduce Retry Cost
sources.koTitle: 배치 재실행 비용을 줄이기 위해 수신과 가공을 분리하는 법
sources.enDescription: Stage external data, rerun internal transformations without repeating provider calls, and reduce the traffic and recovery costs of oversized batch jobs.
sources.koDescription: 외부 데이터를 저장한 뒤 제공자 호출 없이 내부 가공만 재실행해 대형 배치의 트래픽과 복구 비용을 줄이는 방법입니다.

sources.thesis: Exact total-count pagination can consume far more database work than a limited result query, so teams should challenge the requirement and consider slices, cached counts, or estimates.
sources.reason: The body explains a concrete database performance mechanism and connects it to product requirements and operational impact.
risks: Performance depends on database engine, query shape, indexes, statistics, and data distribution, so benchmarks are required.
The Google search example is observational and speculative, not evidence of Google's internal implementation.
The transcript ends with an apparently stray automatic-transcription fragment.

evidence.paraphrase: Unlike a limited query that can stop after enough rows, an exact count must process the full matching set and can consume significant database CPU and memory.
Before building exact totals and last-page navigation, the source recommends product review plus alternatives such as cached counts, separate metadata, or bounded estimates.

sources.enTitle: Why Pagination Count Queries Slow Down Databases
sources.koTitle: 페이징 카운트 쿼리가 데이터베이스를 느리게 하는 이유
sources.enDescription: Understand why exact totals can cost more than limited queries and when to consider slices, cached metadata, estimates, or product changes.
sources.koDescription: 정확한 전체 건수가 제한 조회보다 비싼 이유와 슬라이스, 캐시 메타데이터, 추정치 또는 요구사항 변경을 선택할 기준을 설명합니다.

sources.thesis: Operate distributed services with end-to-end trace correlation and deliberately minimal logs that preserve useful diagnostics without leaking sensitive data or wasting storage.
sources.reason: The source is centrally about observability, distributed tracing, log consistency, privacy, access control, retention, and operational debugging.
risks: Specific Spring tracing library names and maintenance status are uncertain in the transcript and require current documentation checks.
Compliance suggestions are explicitly tentative and require security and legal review.
The blanket advice on production SQL logs needs adaptation for audit, database, and incident-response requirements.

evidence.paraphrase: A request crossing several services needs a shared trace identifier so operators can reconstruct its complete path instead of searching isolated server logs.
Sensitive fields must not leak through generated string representations; log only the minimum useful information while preserving traces needed to operate the service.

sources.enTitle: Design Distributed Tracing and Safe Production Logs Together
sources.koTitle: 분산 추적과 안전한 운영 로그를 함께 설계하는 법
sources.enDescription: Correlate requests across services while controlling log volume, masking sensitive fields, limiting access, and retaining only useful operational data.
sources.koDescription: 서비스 간 요청을 추적하면서 로그 용량, 민감정보 마스킹, 접근 권한과 보관 기간을 함께 설계하는 실무 기준을 다룹니다.

sources.thesis: When a legacy schema is too risky to rename directly, first hide meaningless tables and columns behind repositories and meaningful types, then improve the database after code-level control increases.
sources.reason: The source provides an incremental legacy-data remediation strategy using boundaries, static types, adapters, and staged database change.
risks: The source extrapolates from a brief second-hand description and repeatedly labels the imagined schema details as uncertain.
Adding an abstraction layer can preserve poor schema assumptions if behavior is not first characterized and monitored.
A complete rewrite is mentioned as an alternative for map-heavy dynamic code but not evaluated in depth.

evidence.paraphrase: A repository boundary should hide cryptic table names and expose only meaningful typed results, keeping raw queries and schema vocabulary below the line.
The proposed sequence is to conquer the code first with meaningful classes and isolation, then proceed to database improvement after the bad schema stops leaking outward.

sources.enTitle: Improve a Bad Legacy Schema Behind a Code Boundary
sources.koTitle: 엉망인 레거시 스키마를 코드 경계 뒤에서 개선하는 법
sources.enDescription: Hide cryptic tables behind repositories and meaningful types, regain control in code, then approach improvements to the legacy database.
sources.koDescription: 의미 없는 테이블과 컬럼을 리포지토리와 타입 뒤에 숨겨 코드 통제력을 회복한 뒤 데이터베이스를 점진 개선하는 전략입니다.

sources.thesis: Domain knowledge comes primarily from operating inside a real organization's policies and cross-team problems, and developers prove it through concrete problem-solving rather than vocabulary alone.
sources.reason: The source is a developer career and growth discussion linking domain learning, hiring evidence, technical fundamentals, real operations, and problem-solving ability.
risks: Claims about AI outperforming humans in domain knowledge and hiring-market change are speculative and time-sensitive.
The claim that one must join a company to gain domain knowledge underweights open ecosystems, users, field research, and other operational settings.
Several broad examples and market observations need primary-source verification before publication.

evidence.paraphrase: Real domain knowledge includes company culture, operating rules, and problems among operations, development, and sales; experienced candidates demonstrate how they solved those problems technically.
For entry-level developers, fundamentals and a serious attempt to define and solve realistic problems matter more than claiming domain expertise from a side project.

sources.enTitle: Prove Domain Knowledge Through Real Problem Solving
sources.koTitle: 도메인 지식을 실무 문제 해결로 증명하는 법
sources.enDescription: Domain expertise grows through real operations, policy, and cross-team problems. Show it through concrete problem solving, not terminology alone.
sources.koDescription: 운영, 정책과 부서 간 문제에서 도메인 지식을 쌓고 용어가 아니라 실제 판단과 해결 과정으로 역량을 증명하는 방법을 다룹니다.

sources.thesis: Adopt a new programming language only when its technical advantage outweighs hiring, learning, observability, shared-library, integration, and long-term maintenance costs.
sources.reason: The body is a software technology governance discussion grounded in operating systems after their original authors leave.
risks: Some ecosystem and labor-market claims are explicitly uncertain and geographically specific.
Framework performance comments are broad and require workload-specific benchmarks.
The suggested limit of a few secondary languages is illustrative, not a measured universal threshold.

evidence.paraphrase: A language decision must account for what happens if its small specialist team leaves, whether replacement hiring is possible, and whether the resulting code remains a usable company asset.
Because colleagues must maintain and extend the system after its authors depart, the source argues against uncontrolled language proliferation.

sources.enTitle: Calculate the Full Cost of a New Programming Language
sources.koTitle: 새 프로그래밍 언어 도입의 전체 비용을 계산하는 법
sources.enDescription: Evaluate language adoption through hiring, learning, observability, shared libraries, integration, and maintenance—not technical fit alone.
sources.koDescription: 기술 적합성만 보지 않고 채용, 학습, 관측성, 공통 라이브러리, 통합과 유지보수 비용으로 새 언어 도입을 판단합니다.

sources.thesis: Developers must verify normal behavior before handing work to QA so QA can focus on edge cases and strengthen product quality instead of repeatedly compensating for missing developer tests.
sources.reason: The central purpose is developer quality responsibility and effective collaboration with QA in shipping software.
risks: The source uses stigmatizing labels for developers and treats QA roles somewhat simplistically despite acknowledging organizational variation.
The frequency estimate for irresponsible testing behavior is anecdotal.
Publication should preserve shared quality ownership without implying that every QA ticket is developer failure.

evidence.paraphrase: The rejected pattern is implementing without automated or manual testing and passing work to QA because the developer does not know how to verify it.
Developers should verify minimum cases before handoff so QA can work efficiently, find surprising boundaries, and build mutual trust around product quality.

sources.enTitle: Developer Testing Responsibility Before QA Handoff
sources.koTitle: QA 전달 전에 개발자가 먼저 검증해야 하는 이유
sources.enDescription: Verify expected behavior before QA handoff so testers can pursue edge cases, reduce release loops, and build stronger cross-functional trust.
sources.koDescription: QA 전달 전 개발자가 정상 동작을 검증해 반복 수정 비용을 줄이고 QA가 경계 조건과 제품 품질에 집중하도록 만드는 방법입니다.

sources.thesis: Domain concepts should reflect business importance, hierarchy, and behavior rather than mirroring database tables or generating one repository per entity.
sources.reason: The source is a focused domain-modeling and persistence-boundary discussion using coupon, product, brand, and relationship-table examples.
risks: The product-brand example is underspecified, and the speaker repeatedly revises the interpretation while reasoning aloud.
The on-screen repository and interface sketches are absent from the transcript.
The advice is conceptual and requires concrete transaction, lifecycle, and consistency requirements before implementation.

evidence.paraphrase: One coupon concept may require many supporting tables, establishing that domain count and table count need not match.
A product repository can encapsulate several persistence operations, so neither repositories nor domain concepts need a one-to-one relationship with entities or tables.

sources.enTitle: Why Domain Concepts Should Not Mirror Database Tables
sources.koTitle: 도메인 개념과 데이터베이스 테이블이 일대일이 아닌 이유
sources.enDescription: Model business importance, hierarchy, and behavior instead of creating one domain object and repository for every persistence table.
sources.koDescription: 모든 테이블을 도메인 객체와 리포지토리로 복제하지 않고 비즈니스 중요도, 위계와 행동을 기준으로 모델링하는 법을 설명합니다.

sources.thesis: Discover domain concepts from multiple views of information, behavior, real-world responsibilities, hierarchy, and change instead of treating transport events or every event type as a concept.
sources.reason: The source is centrally a practical domain-modeling method with examples of device signals, grouped behavior, and transport-versus-domain distinctions.
risks: The device-event scenario lacks source details, so the speaker explicitly improvises examples that may not match the questioner's system.
Fire, gas, and access-control behaviors are hypothetical and must not be published as safety-system requirements.
The term event may refer to transport messages or business occurrences, and that ambiguity must remain explicit.

evidence.paraphrase: The speaker uses both information and process views plus real-world observation, warning that a single method can obstruct good software design.
Transport events and protocols are not automatically domain concepts; look for behavioral clusters among types without collapsing everything together or splitting every type apart.

sources.enTitle: Discover Domain Concepts from Information and Behavior
sources.koTitle: 정보와 행동을 함께 보는 도메인 개념 도출법
sources.enDescription: Use information and process or behavior from case-dependent viewpoints to distinguish transport events from domain concepts.
sources.koDescription: 정보와 프로세스 또는 행동을 사례별 관점에서 살펴 전송 이벤트와 도메인 개념을 구분하는 방법입니다.

sources.thesis: Long, exhausting legacy work should be split into small, deployable steps that create early feedback and progress instead of waiting for a perfect rewrite.
sources.reason: The body is centrally about software delivery and legacy-system implementation strategy, including partial traffic migration, repository consolidation, validation, and live deployment.
risks: The company example is deliberately abstracted, so its constraints and validation coverage are incomplete.
Several framework/version and elapsed-time recollections are uncertain or ASR-prone; do not publish them as precise facts.

evidence.paraphrase: 특히 어렵고 힘든 일일수록 ... 일단 일을 쪼개서 하는 방향을 무조건 찾아야 되고 ... 어느 정도는 좀 완벽함을 버릴 줄 알아야 할 것 같아요.
레거시 개편할 때 믿을 수 있는 것 중 하나가 지금 돌아가는 코드 ... 코드 수정을 하나도 안 하면 똑같이 동작 ... 일단은 이걸 병합했던 적이 있거든요.

sources.enTitle: How to Break Long Legacy Migrations into Small, Deployable Steps
sources.koTitle: 긴 레거시 개편을 작은 배포로 나누는 법
sources.enDescription: Break exhausting legacy work into small development, verification, and deployment increments that create feedback before a perfect rewrite.
sources.koDescription: 지치는 레거시 개편을 작은 개발·검증·배포로 나눠 빠르게 피드백을 얻고 완벽주의의 함정을 피하는 방법입니다.

sources.thesis: Use Java Optional at return boundaries where absence is meaningful and the caller must choose a response, not habitually throughout internal fields, parameters, and flows.
sources.reason: The source is an implementation-focused discussion of Java API contracts, nullability, layer boundaries, external calls, and explicit ownership of missing-value handling.
risks: The speaker says he has not used Java recently and offers no compiled code example, so API-level details need independent review.
The guidance is a team convention with acknowledged project-specific exceptions, not a universal Java rule.

evidence.paraphrase: 함수 반환 타입으로 쓸 때 좀 많이 썼던 것 같고 ... 상위 레이어 ... 옵셔널이 없을 수 있게 미리 전처리 같은 걸 한 다음에 넘기는 식으로.
그 책임을 너한테 넘길 거야 말 거야 ... 데이터 조회하는 영역에서 옵셔널을 있게 하자 ... 외부 API 호출한 영역에서 옵셔널이 올 수 있는 거를 지정하자.

sources.enTitle: Java Optional Rules: Keep Absence at Data Boundaries
sources.koTitle: 자바 Optional은 데이터 경계에서만 쓰는 이유
sources.enDescription: Use Java Optional where a missing return value gives callers a real choice, while keeping fields, parameters, and trusted internal flows explicit.
sources.koDescription: 값의 부재를 호출자가 실제로 결정해야 하는 반환 경계에서만 Optional을 쓰고 내부 흐름은 명확하게 유지하는 기준입니다.

sources.thesis: Design account-deletion data flows around explicit retention policy, operational recovery needs, and genuine storage separation, with legal and audit experts defining the current rules.
sources.reason: Its central purpose is operating data systems for real users: moving retained orders, handling cancellation and re-registration, separating storage, encrypting identifiers, and expiring records.
risks: The speaker repeatedly states he is not a legal expert; all retention periods and separation requirements require current counsel or auditor confirmation.
The dormant-account discussion is recalled and checked informally during recording, so it must not be presented as current law.

evidence.paraphrase: 저도 법령 전문가는 아니고 ... 제가 겪었던 논리적 물리적 분리된 DB를 의미 ... 스키마만 분리하는 게 아니라 DBMS 자체를 별도로 만들어가지고 옮겨거리는 게 사실 베스트.
법안이나 정책들 ... 계속 바뀌기 때문에 전문가분들이 ... 해석 ... 외부 기관 ... 가이드를 ... 그거 맞춰서 하는 게 제일 심플.

sources.enTitle: Account Deletion Data: Retention, Separation, and Recovery Design
sources.koTitle: 회원 탈퇴 데이터의 보관·분리·복구 설계
sources.enDescription: Design deleted-account data around verified retention rules, isolated storage, encryption, expiry, and the operational flows that may still need recovery.
sources.koDescription: 탈퇴 회원 데이터를 검증된 보관 기준, 분리 저장, 암호화, 만료와 취소·재가입 같은 운영 흐름에 맞춰 설계합니다.

sources.thesis: Judge code review health by whether early feedback aligns a team and declines over time, using automation and draft pull requests to surface mismatches before work hardens.
sources.reason: The body is about developer collaboration, onboarding, asynchronous review, team conventions, and automating mechanical checks rather than chasing a raw review-comment count.
risks: Comment counts are only a proxy: few comments may mean alignment or superficial review, and many comments vary in substance.
The draft-PR workflow assumes a team willing and able to review unfinished work promptly.

evidence.paraphrase: 이런 문제를 좀 해결을 하는 거에 가장 좋은 거는 ... 드래프트 PR ... 작은 일부터 서로 동기화 ... 리뷰가 많이 나오다가 점점점점 줄어드는 그 추이를 보는 게 더 중요.
드래프트 PR 같은 걸 활용하면서 ... 리뷰를 점점 줄여가는 거를 목표 ... 작업하는 중간에 먼저 피드백을 드릴 수 있기 때문에.

sources.enTitle: Code Review Health Is a Trend, Not a Comment Count
sources.koTitle: 코드 리뷰 품질은 댓글 수보다 줄어드는 추이로 본다
sources.enDescription: Use automation and draft pull requests to align teammates early, then track whether repeated feedback declines as shared conventions become real practice.
sources.koDescription: 자동화와 드래프트 PR로 초기에 합을 맞추고, 공통 규칙이 자리 잡으며 반복 피드백이 줄어드는지를 확인합니다.

sources.thesis: Build a developer career by identifying a distinctive strength mix, testing preferences through real or side-project experience, and repeatedly revising a concrete future direction.
sources.reason: The source centrally addresses developer growth and career design through self-assessment, team contribution, varied backend roles, experiments, and deliberate five- and ten-year reflection.
risks: The strength model and daily reflection cadence are personal heuristics, not validated assessment methods.
The later predictions about AI and future work are speculative and should not anchor a publication.

evidence.paraphrase: 한 가지 뚜렷한 강력한 장점과 두 가지 뭉툭한 장점 ... 내가 코드를 ... 일을 추진 ... 복잡한 도메인을 이해 ... 동료들한테 물어보는 것도 방법.
좋아하는 것을 찾으려면 사실 한 번씩 해보긴 해야 돼요 ... 사이드 프로젝트 ... 오픈소스 ... 내가 서비스 향으로 해서 어떤 사람한테 가치를 좀 직접적으로 주는 걸 좋아하는구나.

sources.enTitle: Design Your Developer Career Around Strengths and Experiments
sources.koTitle: 강점과 실험으로 개발자 커리어를 설계하는 법
sources.enDescription: Map your strongest capabilities, test different kinds of engineering work, and keep revising a future direction from evidence rather than vague ambition.
sources.koDescription: 자신의 강점을 구조화하고 여러 개발 경험을 직접 시험하며, 막연한 포부 대신 근거로 미래 방향을 계속 고치는 방법입니다.

sources.thesis: Engineering leadership should formalize responsibility, results, and peer trust already demonstrated in practice rather than grant authority first and hope capability follows.
sources.reason: The body focuses on developer leadership growth: code review, incident response, company-wide problem solving, readiness for opportunity, and trust from close collaborators.
risks: The model is explicitly drawn from the speaker's experience in relatively healthy organizations and may not fit political or appointment-driven structures.
Acting beyond one's role can become unpaid or unsupported labor unless scope, authority, and recognition are made explicit.

evidence.paraphrase: 이미 리더 역할을 하고 있을 때 리더가 된다. 사실은 오늘 말하고 싶은 거에 결론.
그 팀장 일을 하고 계시면 됩니다 ... 팀장의 역할을 대행할 수 있는 수준의 역량과 결과물과 그 동료들의 신뢰를 받았을 때 ... 다음 기회.

sources.enTitle: Engineering Leadership Starts Before the Title
sources.koTitle: 개발 리더십은 직함을 받기 전에 시작된다
sources.enDescription: Prepare for engineering leadership by already handling reviews, incidents, broad problems, and peer trust before an organization adds the formal title.
sources.koDescription: 리뷰, 장애, 넓은 문제와 동료의 신뢰를 먼저 책임지며 직함이 붙기 전부터 개발 리더십을 준비하는 기준입니다.

sources.thesis: When immediate financial constraints allow, evaluate a developer job by the domain, operating problems, and learning material you can actively turn into future capability—not salary alone.
sources.reason: The source is a developer-career decision framework grounded in choosing exposure to B2C, global delivery, finance, operations, and different organizational scales.
risks: The advice is personal and explicitly conditional; salary, stability, caregiving, and market constraints can rightly dominate a decision.
An interesting domain does not guarantee access to the desired work, mentors, or operating responsibility.

evidence.paraphrase: 돈을 더 준다고 했었는데도 ... 결국은 경험, 경험치 그리고 이제 성장의 재료 ... 실제 이 서비스를 해본 거랑 또 차원이 다르기 때문에.
당장의 이익보다도 경험을 항상 중심으로 하시는 게 멀리 갈 때 기준으로 유리하지 않을까 ... 이직 자체가 되게 쉬운 시장 상황은 아니.

sources.enTitle: Choose Your Next Developer Job for Experience, Not Salary Alone
sources.koTitle: 개발자 이직은 연봉만이 아니라 다음 경험으로 고른다
sources.enDescription: Compare developer jobs by the domains, operating problems, and responsibilities you can turn into lasting capability, while respecting real financial constraints.
sources.koDescription: 현실적인 금전 제약을 존중하면서도 도메인, 운영 문제, 책임을 장기 역량으로 바꿀 수 있는지를 이직 기준에 넣습니다.

sources.thesis: Migrate a legacy database by inserting a compatible adapter, deploying dormant paths early, dual-writing behind flags, testing each state, switching reads deliberately, and deleting retired code.
sources.reason: This is a detailed production migration case covering Oracle-to-MySQL query conversion, adapter boundaries, dual writes, toggles, DBA-assisted data movement, rollback, testing, and cleanup.
risks: The example code is reconstructed from memory and many flag, class, and query names are garbled by ASR; publish the mechanism, not those identifiers.
Dual writes introduce consistency and reconciliation risks that the transcript does not fully specify; a real design needs failure handling and measurable parity checks.

evidence.paraphrase: 서비스 쪽 로직을 하나도 수정을 안 했어요 ... 서비스 쪽 로직을 수정하는 순간 ... 우려 ... 그래서 그대로 다 어댑팅하는 전략.
이 안에서만 모든 작업을 끝내면 ... 데이터베이스를 천천히 페이드아웃 ... 듀얼라이트 ... 미리 사전에 다 배포 ... 검증 ... 스위치만 딱 킨 식.

sources.enTitle: Oracle to MySQL Migration with Adapters, Dual Writes, and Flags
sources.koTitle: 어댑터·듀얼 라이트·플래그로 Oracle을 MySQL로 이관하기
sources.enDescription: A reversible Oracle-to-MySQL migration using compatible adapters, dormant deployments, dual writes, tested switches, deliberate rollback, and legacy cleanup.
sources.koDescription: 호환 어댑터, 사전 배포, 듀얼 라이트, 검증된 스위치와 롤백으로 Oracle 레거시를 MySQL로 점진 이관합니다.

sources.thesis: Choose career diversity that matches the engineer you want to become: broader leadership ambitions may benefit from smaller-company constraints, while deep specialists may choose scale and focus.
sources.reason: The central purpose is developer career growth through deliberate exposure to different scales, problem sizes, imperfect teams, and kinds of responsibility.
risks: The source generalizes sharply from a limited personal sample and explicitly acknowledges counterexamples.
Hardship is not inherently educational; poor management, exploitation, or unsafe work should not be romanticized as required experience.

evidence.paraphrase: 나는 5년 뒤에 CTO ... 창업 ... 뛰어난 시니어 엔지니어 ... 다 다를 거잖아요 ... CTO나 어떤 창업 ... 작은 회사나 스타트업 같은 곳에 한번 가보라.
더 큰 일 더 큰 규모와 더 다양한 걸 하고 싶다 ... 다양성을 늘려야 ... 기술 장인이 되고 싶어요 이런 사람들은 사실 비추.

sources.enTitle: Build Engineering Career Range Across Company Sizes
sources.koTitle: 회사 규모를 넘나들며 개발자 경험의 폭을 넓히는 법
sources.enDescription: Match company scale to your long-term path: broaden operating and leadership experience when needed, or preserve focus when deep technical craft is the goal.
sources.koDescription: 장기 목표에 맞춰 작은 조직의 넓은 책임과 큰 조직의 깊은 전문성 중 필요한 경험의 폭을 의도적으로 선택합니다.

sources.thesis: Do not let an admin-facing common module become the owner of every domain; preserve service boundaries and tolerate small duplication until genuinely shared behavior and lifecycle emerge.
sources.reason: The body is a software architecture analysis of admin requirements, multi-module dependencies, domain ownership, common-module coupling, and exceptions where admin itself is the product.
risks: The original project structure is incomplete, and the speaker repeatedly labels his module-topology reconstruction as an assumption.
Admin products and stable shared persistence capabilities may justify different boundaries than internal operational screens.

evidence.paraphrase: 어드민은 이제 커먼이라고 만들었어요 ... 모든 기능들 ... 서비스 1, 2, 3 ... 어드민 커먼을 보고 ... 안 좋게 역전 ... 커먼이 모든 도메인을 다 알고.
어드민의 요구사항의 차이 ... 커먼에 ... 각각 ... 그렇게 될 바에는 ... 조금 중복 코드가 있어봐도 ... 각각 명확하게 분리.

sources.enTitle: Avoid the Admin Common Module That Owns Every Domain
sources.koTitle: 모든 도메인을 삼키는 어드민 공통 모듈을 피하라
sources.enDescription: Keep admin features from reversing domain dependencies. Preserve service boundaries and accept small duplication while admin requirements continue to diverge.
sources.koDescription: 어드민 요구가 도메인 의존성을 뒤집지 않게 서비스 경계를 지키고, 요구가 계속 갈라지는 동안 작은 중복을 허용합니다.

sources.thesis: Turn tacit engineering rules into a lightweight, reviewable convention that explains current choices, allows team overrides, supports onboarding, and stays alive through shared edits.
sources.reason: Although the opening and ending mention a course, the central body is developer collaboration and software stewardship through conventions, onboarding sessions, repository docs, team review, and AI instructions.
risks: The transcript repeatedly renders '암묵지' as '안목지'; normalize the concept without claiming the ASR wording is exact.
Documentation can become stale or coercive; the source itself favors loose company defaults, explicit team overrides, and selective maintenance.

evidence.paraphrase: 신규 입사자한테 온보딩 ... AI한테 이 프로젝트를 어떻게 수정 ... 팀 리포에 문서를 ... 팀 안에서 협의가 되면 무조건 여기에 적어 ... 팀에서 결정을 했다면 ... 오버라이드.
전사 기준으로 정리 ... 직원이 몇 천명인데 ... 말이 안 되거든요 ... 메인 컨벤션 느슨한 컨벤션을 만들어 놓고 팀마다 ... 커스텀.

sources.enTitle: Turn Tacit Engineering Rules into Living Team Conventions
sources.koTitle: 암묵지를 살아 있는 팀 컨벤션으로 만드는 법
sources.enDescription: Document the engineering rules teammates carry in their heads, explain why they exist, permit team overrides, and keep them alive through review and onboarding.
sources.koDescription: 팀원의 머릿속에만 있는 개발 규칙을 이유와 함께 기록하고, 팀별 재정의와 리뷰·온보딩으로 살아 있게 관리합니다.

sources.thesis: Start entity relationships with the simplest cardinality that fits current requirements, but treat proven decision volatility, unchanged deadlines, and team context as legitimate design inputs.
sources.reason: The central discussion is domain and data relationship design under real implementation constraints, using one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many choices as the concrete problem.
risks: Choosing many-to-many preemptively can still encode the wrong domain and add unnecessary implementation complexity.
The organizational examples are anecdotal; 'leaders often change requirements' should be established from local evidence, not assumed.

evidence.paraphrase: 회사 내부의 현실적인 상황도 ... 결정을 ... 대부분 경우에 1대1, 1대N으로 접근 ... 예기치 못하는 상황 ... N대N ... 의사 결정권자가 ... 의견을 계속 뒤집 ... N대N 쓰는 게 맞다.
개발자들만의 관점으로는 ... 설계를 구축하는 게 ... 실제 회사에서는 ... 회사마다 사실은 ... 설계 스타일도 달라지는 것.

sources.enTitle: Design Data Relationships for Organizational Reality
sources.koTitle: 조직 현실까지 고려한 데이터 관계 설계
sources.enDescription: Prefer simple relationship cardinality, then account for observed requirement churn, decision habits, and deadline constraints instead of predicting every future change.
sources.koDescription: 단순한 관계에서 시작하되 실제 요구사항 변경, 의사결정 습관과 일정 제약을 관찰해 데이터 관계 설계에 반영합니다.

sources.thesis: Improve a weak engineering culture by first learning the organization and earning trust, then creating small team practices whose visible quality and delivery gains attract wider adoption.
sources.reason: The source is centrally about developer responsibility and collaboration: entering a new company, introducing tests and policy discussions, working with product peers, and spreading change through demonstrated outcomes.
risks: The claimed success rate is an anecdotal estimate, not measured evidence, and should be omitted.
Bottom-up change may fail in hostile or entrenched power structures; the source itself says leaving can be the better choice.

evidence.paraphrase: 최소 3개월은 관망 ... 귀는 열고 입은 닫자 ... 신뢰를 얻자 ... 개발자 플러스 비개발자 ... 그 다음에 의견을 피력.
내 팀 먼저 바꾸는 걸 해야 돼요 ... 옆 팀이 관심 ... 실제 실무에 대한 걸 해결 ... 자기 팀도 하고 싶은데 어떻게 하면 좋은지.

sources.enTitle: Change Engineering Culture Through Trust and Small Wins
sources.koTitle: 신뢰와 작은 성공으로 개발 문화를 바꾸는 법
sources.enDescription: Learn a new organization before prescribing fixes, earn trust through delivery, and let visible gains from tests and shared policy work spread beyond your team.
sources.koDescription: 새 조직을 먼저 이해하고 일로 신뢰를 얻은 뒤, 테스트와 정책 공유의 작은 성과를 보여 개발 문화를 확산합니다.

sources.thesis: Maintain a small, trusted documentation set covering policy, core concepts, system flows, and API contracts rather than producing many artifacts that drift apart and lose credibility.
sources.reason: The body addresses sustainable developer collaboration and operating handover through requirements and policy documents, concept and system diagrams, batch flows, API docs, ownership, and onboarding feedback.
risks: The proposed document set is a heuristic and must vary with system complexity, regulation, team topology, and operational risk.
A smaller set still fails without clear ownership and change-triggered updates; consolidating too aggressively can erase necessary detail.

evidence.paraphrase: 가능한 최소한의 문서 ... 문서가 많으면 ... 관리 비용 ... 최신화가 계속 안 돼 있는 문서는 ... 볼 수가 없는.
요구사항 정의서 정책서 ... 개념도 ... 시스템 링크 ... 문서 이거 3개 정도 ... 관리하기도 쉬워 ... 유사한 문서가 많으면 ... 관리가 점점 힘들어.

sources.enTitle: Keep a Small Documentation Set the Team Can Trust
sources.koTitle: 팀이 믿을 수 있는 최소 문서만 최신화하라
sources.enDescription: Reduce documentation sprawl by maintaining a trusted core of policy, concepts, system flows, and API contracts with clear ownership and onboarding feedback.
sources.koDescription: 정책, 핵심 개념, 시스템 흐름과 API 계약을 소수의 신뢰할 문서로 관리하고 온보딩 피드백으로 계속 최신화합니다.

sources.thesis: Keep an honest employment history, but tailor emphasis and project detail to each role so an unusual background becomes credible evidence of the value you can deliver.
sources.reason: The body is about developer hiring and career communication: truthful resumes, role-specific versions, job-description alignment, interview narrative, and converting adjacent AI experience into relevant evidence.
risks: The source initially explores omitting experience but later rejects career reduction; publication must preserve the final honesty constraint and avoid contradictory advice.
Claims about employment records and hiring consequences are not legal guidance and should be checked for the target jurisdiction and employer.

evidence.paraphrase: 원래는 하면 안 됩니다 ... 경력을 과대포장하는 것도 문제지만 축소하는 것도 ... 사람이 전체에 지나온 시간이 결국 그 사람을 만든다 ... 써야 된다.
AI를 조금 강조한 버전과 ... 강조하지 않은 버전 ... 경력은 그대로 적고 ... 회사마다 이력서를 내용을 다 바꾸셔야 ... 경력이나 이런 거 중심으로 내가 어필.

sources.enTitle: Turn an Unusual Developer Background into an Interview Strength
sources.koTitle: 애매한 개발 경력을 정직한 면접 강점으로 바꾸는 법
sources.enDescription: Keep your full work history honest, then tailor project emphasis to each role so adjacent experience gives interviewers credible reasons to hire you.
sources.koDescription: 전체 경력은 정직하게 유지하되 지원 역할마다 프로젝트 강조점을 바꿔, 인접 경험을 채용할 만한 근거로 만듭니다.

sources.thesis: Keep volatile display policy and experiment decisions on the server for long-lived app versions, while translating them at the presentation boundary so core business concepts stay clean.
sources.reason: The source is an API-design discussion about app backward compatibility, server-controlled formatting and badges, experiments, client contracts, and separation between presentation and domain logic.
risks: The old-app usage evidence is anecdotal and undated; the architectural argument should not depend on a specific update-rate claim.
Returning every field as a string is presented as an observed alternative, not the recommended design, and can weaken type safety.

evidence.paraphrase: 클라이언트의 로직이 있을만한 것과 서버 쪽에서 해줘야 되는 것들 ... 프레젠테이션 레이어 ... 클라이언트를 위한 레이어 ... 프레젠테이션 레이어와 개념 영역을 잘 분리.
비즈니스 로직 쪽에서 내려줄 때는 ... 15,000을 그대로 내려주고 API 리스폰스 할 때만 ... 클라이언트가 원하는 대로 ... 도메인과 개념 영역의 데이터를 변환.

sources.enTitle: Server-Driven API Responses for Mobile App Compatibility
sources.koTitle: 앱 하위 호환성을 위한 서버 주도 API 응답 설계
sources.enDescription: Keep changing display policy and experiments server-side for old app versions, but isolate that translation at the API boundary to protect the domain model.
sources.koDescription: 구버전 앱을 위해 변하는 표시 정책과 실험은 서버가 맡되, 변환을 API 경계에 격리해 도메인 모델을 보호합니다.

sources.thesis: Replace all-in-one company libraries with composable modules so each service declares only the infrastructure it needs, understands its dependency graph, and avoids hidden runtime cost and failure coupling.
sources.reason: The body is a detailed software architecture and developer-tooling argument about Gradle dependencies, Redis and Kafka coupling, auto-configuration, composable modules, presets, testing modules, and framework upgrades.
risks: Spring Boot 4 module details are described while browsing on-screen code and include ASR-corrupted names; verify all framework claims against official source before publication.
Fine-grained modules add discovery and assembly cost; the source allows documented higher-level presets when team skill or delivery speed justifies them.

evidence.paraphrase: 의존성을 거는 순간 모든 의존성이 다 들어와요 ... 내가 안 써도 ... 쓸데없이 자원을 쓰는 ... 소프트웨어가 무거워 ... 충돌 가능성 ... 생각지도 못한 데서 영향.
조합 가능한 구조 ... 로깅 모듈 ... JPA나 카프카 ... 모듈로 다 별개로 나눠 ... 선 넘지 않는 구조.

sources.enTitle: Split All-in-One Libraries into Composable Dependency Modules
sources.koTitle: 통 라이브러리를 조합 가능한 의존성 모듈로 쪼개라
sources.enDescription: Avoid hidden infrastructure, runtime cost, and dependency conflicts by splitting company libraries into modules each service can understand and compose deliberately.
sources.koDescription: 전사 통 라이브러리를 서비스가 이해하고 선택할 수 있는 모듈로 나눠 숨은 인프라 연결, 자원 낭비와 의존성 충돌을 막습니다.
